text:
Valeri Nichushkin was a Cup winner and a play driver in Colorado; in Columbus, so far, he's been a quieter version. Nine points in 16 games, two goals, and the Blue Jackets are about even in chances at five on five with him on.

The reason to stay patient is last season. Evolving-Hockey had him 47th of 401 forwards in wins above replacement, in the 87th percentile for driving offense and the 89th for taking chances away. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking liked his puck work: 64% of his exits with possession and 55% of his entries carried in. Those habits don't vanish with a change of sweater.

What has vanished, for now, is the shot volume: 1.1 expected goals in his last ten games. His ice time is creeping up, though, and he scored the shootout winner against Dallas. Our range has him at 41 to 63 points, which would be a fine first season in Ohio.
